arxiv-1404-2981.title: On free stable distributions
arxiv-1404-2981.creator: T. Hasebe, A. Kuznetsov
arxiv-1404-2981.description: Abstract We investigate analytical properties of free stable distributions and discover many connections with their classical counterparts. Our main result is an explicit formula for the Mellin transform, which leads to explicit series representations for the characteristic function and for the density of a free stable distribution.

arxiv-1910-07269.title: “Get a Free Item Pack with Every Activation!”
arxiv-1910-07269.creator: *, Sabrina Amft, Daniel Hecker, Emanuel von Zezschwitz
arxiv-1910-07269.description: Abstract Account security is an ongoing issue in practice. Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) is a mechanism which could help mitigate this problem, however adoption is not very high in most domains. Online gaming has adopted an interesting approach to drive adoption: Games offer small rewards such as visual modifications to the player’s avatar’s appearance, if players utilize 2FA.

arxiv-2107-13283.title: Superconducting Properties of La 1.85 Sr 0.15 CuO 4 - Sr 2 IrO 4 multilayers
arxiv-2107-13283.creator: Himanshu Pandey 1∗ , Manoj Kumar 2 , D. Tripathi 2 , and S. Pandey 1
arxiv-2107-13283.description: Abstract We study superconducting properties in multilayer thin films consisting of superconducting La 1.85 Sr 0.15 CuO 4 (LSCO) and Mott insulator Sr 2 IrO 4 (SIO) and report enhanced superconductivity in optimized sample. These multilayer heterostructures show an increase in superconducting transition temperature ( T C T_{C} ) as compared to the single layer LSCO films.

arxiv-2111-12645.title: Searching for Yang-Lee zeros in O( N N ) models
arxiv-2111-12645.creator: Jan M. Pawlowski
arxiv-2111-12645.description: Abstract Near the second order phase transition point, QCD with two flavours of massless quarks can be approximated by an O( 4 4 ) model, where a symmetry breaking external field H H can be added to play the role of quark mass.

arxiv-2201-06107.title: Comparison of spin-correlation and polarization variables of spin density matrix for top quark pairs at the LHC and New Physics implications
arxiv-2201-06107.creator: Altan Cakir, and Orcun Kolay
arxiv-2201-06107.description: Abstract Precise determination of top-quark pairs is an essential tool for understanding the overall consistency of the standard model (SM) expectations, understanding limited New Physics (NP) models, through spin-spin correlation and polarization parameters, and has a critical impact on the analyses strategies at upcoming LHC programs.

arxiv-2207-11879.title: A Robust Optimization Framework for Two-Echelon Vehicle and UAV Routing for Post-Disaster Humanitarian Logistics Operations Corresponding author. Email: mnalam@neu.edu.
arxiv-2207-11879.creator: Tasnim Ibn Faiz
arxiv-2207-11879.description: Abstract Providing first aid and other supplies (e.g., epi-pens, medical supplies, dry food, water) during and after a disaster is always challenging. The complexity of these operations increases when the transportation, power, and communications networks fail, leaving people stranded and unable to communicate their locations and needs.

arxiv-2209-15323.title: SmallCap : Lightweight Image Captioning Prompted with Retrieval Augmentation
arxiv-2209-15323.creator: Rita Ramos Bruno Martins Desmond Elliott Yova Kementchedjhieva
arxiv-2209-15323.description: Abstract Recent advances in image captioning have focused on scaling the data and model size, substantially increasing the cost of pre-training and finetuning. As an alternative to large models, we present SmallCap , which generates a caption conditioned on an input image and related captions retrieved from a datastore.

arxiv-2212-06190.title: IrF 4 : From Tetrahedral Compass Model to Topological Semimetal
arxiv-2212-06190.creator: Chao Shang, Owen Ganter, Niclas Heinsdorf, Stephen M. Winter
arxiv-2212-06190.description: Abstract The intersection of topology, symmetry, and magnetism yields a rich structure of possible phases. In this work, we study theoretically the consequences of magnetism on IrF 4 , which was recently identified as a possible candidate topological nodal chain semimetal in the absence of magnetic order.

arxiv-2303-02005.title: The turnpike property for mean-field optimal control problems
arxiv-2303-02005.creator: Martin Gugat, Michael Herty, Chiara Segala
arxiv-2303-02005.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Martin Gugat, Michael Herty, Chiara Segala. We study the turnpike phenomenon for optimal control problems with mean field dynamics that are obtained as the limit N → ∞ N\rightarrow\infty of systems governed by a large number N N of ordinary differential equations. We show that the optimal control problems with with large time horizons give rise to a turnpike structure of the optimal state and the optimal control.

arxiv-2406-19779.title: Structuring in Thin Films during Meniscus-Guided Deposition
arxiv-2406-19779.creator: René de Bruijn, Anton A. Darhuber, Jasper J. Michels, Paul van der Schoot
arxiv-2406-19779.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by René de Bruijn, Anton A. Darhuber, Jasper J. Michels, Paul van der Schoot. We study theoretically the evaporation-driven phase separation of a binary fluid mixture in a thin film deposited on a moving substrate, as occurs in meniscus-guided deposition for solution-processed materials. Our focus is on rapid substrate motion during, where phase separation takes place far removed from the coating device under conditions where the mixture is essentially stationary with respect to the substrate.

arxiv-2408-01567.title: Terahertz high-harmonic generation in gapped antiferromagnetic chains
arxiv-2408-01567.creator: Mohsen Yarmohammadi, Michael H. Kolodrubetz
arxiv-2408-01567.description: Abstract The nonlinear dynamics of magnetization in antiferromagnets, resulting in high-frequency spin waves (high-order harmonics) as signal carriers, enable fast magnetic state switching in spintronic devices. More harmonic orders potentially allow more information to be conveyed by the spins. Developing theoretical models to describe these waves in antiferromagnets is essential for predicting their properties and guiding experimental efforts.

arxiv-2409-05171.title: Exploring Fungal Morphology Simulation and Dynamic Light Containment from a Graphics Generation Perspective DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: SIGGRAPH Asia 2024 Art Papers; December 03–06, 2024; Tokyo, Japan SIGGRAPH Asia 2024 Art Papers (SA Art Papers ’24), December 03–06, 2024, Tokyo, Japan ISBN: 9
arxiv-2409-05171.creator: Kexin Wang, Ivy He, Jinke Li, Ali Asadipour, Yitong Sun
arxiv-2409-05171.description: Abstract . Fungal simulation and control are considered crucial techniques in Bio-Art creation. However, coding algorithms for reliable fungal simulations have posed significant challenges for artists. This study equates fungal morphology simulation to a two-dimensional graphic time-series generation problem. We propose a zero-coding, neural network-driven cellular automaton.

arxiv-2506-05018.title: Observation of t ​ t ¯ ​ γ ​ γ t\bar{t}\gamma\gamma production at s = \sqrt{s}= 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-2506-05018.description: Abstract This paper presents the first observation of top-quark pair production in association with two photons ( t ​ t ¯ ​ γ ​ γ t\bar{t}\gamma\gamma ). The measurement is performed in the single-lepton decay channel using proton–proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider.

arxiv-2506-23476.title: Probing the structure of exotic hadrons through correlation functions
arxiv-2506-23476.creator: Yi-bo Shen, Zhi-Wei Liu, Jun-Xu Lu, Ming-Zhu Liu, Li-Sheng Geng
arxiv-2506-23476.description: Abstract Over the past 20 years, many new hadron states have been discovered, but understanding their nature remains a key experimental and theoretical challenge. Recent studies have established that hadron-hadron interactions primarily govern the generation of new hadronic states, with their spectroscopy serving as a powerful tool for probing these interactions and determining the corresponding compositeness.

arxiv-2507-05118.title: VerifyLLM: LLM-Based Pre-Execution Task Plan Verification for Robots
arxiv-2507-05118.creator: Danil S. Grigorev, Alexey K. Kovalev, Aleksandr I. Panov
arxiv-2507-05118.description: Abstract In the field of robotics, researchers face a critical challenge in ensuring reliable and efficient task planning. Verifying high-level task plans before execution significantly reduces errors and enhance the overall performance of these systems. In this paper, we propose an architecture for automatically verifying high-level task plans before their execution in simulator or real-world environments.

arxiv-2510-25985.title: A New Type of Axis–Angle Attitude Control Law for Rotational Systems: Synthesis, Analysis, and Experiments Thanks: The research presented in this paper was supported by the Joint Center for Aerospace Technology Innovation (JCATI) through Award 172 172 , the Washington State University (WSU) Foundati
arxiv-2510-25985.creator: Francisco M. F. R. Gonçalves, Ryan M. Bena, Néstor O. Pérez-Arancibia
arxiv-2510-25985.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Francisco M. F. R. Gonçalves, Ryan M. Bena, Néstor O. Pérez-Arancibia. Over the past few decades, continuous quaternion-based attitude control has been proven highly effective for driving rotational systems that can be modeled as rigid bodies, such as satellites and drones.

arxiv-2606-16831.creator: Philipp Mohr, Jasper Brüggmann, Viet Hoang Le, and Gerhard Bauch

pmc-10548758.title: Arts-based therapies, practices, and interventions in health
pmc-10548758.creator: Theresa Van Lith, Mark Ettenberger
pmc-10548758.description: This collection focuses on creative art therapies, practices, and interventions in health contexts as part of the Mind-body interventions series of BMC Complementary Medicine and Therapies. The collection highlights the emerging value of the arts in complementary medicine and contributes to the expanding knowledge and integration of mind-body interventions and creative art practices.

pmc-10609424.title: Capillary Underfill Flow Simulation as a Design Tool for Flow-Optimized Encapsulation in Heterogenous Integration †
pmc-10609424.creator: Lisa Christin Stencel, Jörg Strogies, Bernd Müller, Rüdiger Knofe, Carsten Borwieck, Matthias Heimann
pmc-10609424.description: As the power electronics landscape evolves, pushing for greater vertical integration, capillary underfilling is considered a versatile encapsulation technique suited for iterative development cycles of innovative integration concepts. Since a defect-free application is critical, this study proposes a capillary two-phase flow simulation, predicting both the flow pattern and velocity with remarkable precision and efficiency.

pmc-11443326.title: Progressive Impairment of Cardiac Autonomic Regulation as the Number of Metabolic Syndrome Components Increases
pmc-11443326.creator: Daniela Lucini, Luca Giovanelli, Mara Malacarne, Giuseppina Bernardelli, Alessandro Ardigò, Wolfgang Gatzemeier, Nadia Solaro
pmc-11443326.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMetabolic syndrome (MetS) is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular diseases. Compelling evidence supports the key role of dysfunction in the autonomic nervous system in that association, as well as mutual correlation among the components of MetS. The autonomic nervous system index (ANSI) is a percentile-ranked unitary proxy of cardiac autonomic regulation (CAR) that is designed to be free of age and sex bias, with higher values indicating better autonomic control.

pmc-11500544.title: Sequencing and phylogenetic analysis of the complete mitochondrial genome of the Eurasian Harvest Mouse (Micromys minutus) Pallas 1771 from China
pmc-11500544.creator: Hong-Yan Wang, Yu-Qi Wu, Zhi-Hui Zhang, Zhu Liu
pmc-11500544.description: This study aimed to examine the complete mitochondrial genome sequence of the Eurasian Harvest Mouse (Micromys minutus) through polymerase chain reaction. The mitochondrial genome of M. minutus was characterized as a circular, double-stranded DNA molecule, encompassing a total length of 16,239 bp. The mitochondrial genome composition of M.

pmc-12575792.title: Differential effects of human density, environmental health, and group size on urban coyote detection, boldness, and exploration
pmc-12575792.creator: Cesar O. Estien, Lauren A. Stanton, Christopher J. Schell
pmc-12575792.description: Comparative studies show that urban coyotes behave differently from rural counterparts. However, these studies often homogenize cities. Cities feature diverse pressures for wildlife, such as variation in human densities and environmental health, two factors known to increase risk-taking. This heterogeneity creates a landscape of risk, which may drive locally adapted behavioral strategies within cities.

pmc-12614554.title: Building a continuous benchmarking ecosystem in bioinformatics
pmc-12614554.creator: Izaskun Mallona, Charlotte Soneson, Ben Carrillo, Almut Lütge, Daniel Incicau, Reto Gerber, Anthony Sonrel, Mark D. Robinson
pmc-12614554.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Benchmarking, which involves collecting reference datasets and demonstrating method performance, is a requirement for the development of new computational tools, but also becomes a domain of its own to achieve neutral comparisons of methods. Although a lot has been written about how to design and conduct benchmark studies, this Perspective sheds light on a wish list for a computational platform to orchestrate benchmark studies.

pmc-13063331.title: Emotion regulation skills training as an adjunctive treatment to narrative exposure therapy for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in refugees: a pilot randomized controlled trial
pmc-13063331.creator: Angela Nickerson, Marylene Cloitre, Frank Neuner, Meaghan O'Donnell, Richard A. Bryant, Belinda J. Liddell, Avalon Tissue, Stephanie Murphy, Casey Willoughby, Joel Hoffman, Yulisha Byrow, Shivani Uppal, Natalie Mastrogiovanni, Natalie Peach, Sarah Funnell, Vivian Mai, Marta Gurzeda, Jenny J.Y. Im, G
pmc-13063331.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Responses to evidence-based interventions for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in refugees vary considerably. Emotion regulation difficulties are associated with greater PTSD severity in refugees and thus represent a potential treatment target.Objective: This study aimed to test the efficacy of Skills Training in Affective and Interpersonal Regulation for Refugees (STAIR-R) and Narrative Exposure Therapy (NET) or Supportive Problem-Solving (SPS) and NET.

pmc-13146874.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A983 POSITIONAL OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA IS A PREDOMINANT PHENOTYPE IN ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE: ASSOCIATIONS WITH DISEASE SEVERITY AND IMPLICATIONS FOR MANAGEMENT
pmc-13146874.creator: Tho Phung, Giap Vu, Hoai Nguyen
pmc-13146874.description: Background and aimsObstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is highly prevalent during the acute phase of ischemic stroke and is associated with adverse neurological outcomes. Supine positioning is common after stroke and may exacerbate respiratory events. Positional OSA (POSA) represents a potentially modifiable phenotype, but its characteristics in the acute stroke setting remain insufficiently described.

pmc-13396433.title: Inflammatory and Oxidative Stress Biomarkers in Gingival Crevicular Fluid (GCF) and Serum of Dogs With Gingivitis and Periodontitis
pmc-13396433.creator: Doğu Turgut, Efe Kurtdede, Hannah Wesley
pmc-13396433.description: Introduction/ObjectivesPeriodontal disease is one of the most common oral disorders in dogs and is characterized by inflammation and destruction of periodontal tissues. This study aimed to compare local and systemic inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers in dogs with gingivitis and periodontitis and to evaluate neopterin as a potential biomarker of periodontal inflammation.

pmc-13402802.title: Fluorescence localization and tracking imaging with a spectral-splitting perovskite single-pixel detector
pmc-13402802.creator: Yujin Liu, Hongling Wan, Xinyu Yin, Zhihao Zhang, Jingjing Liu, Jingyang Xing, Hao Wang, Hanyan Zhao, Jieyu Tian, Xianping He, Jiaqi Wei, Zhong Ji, Xueli Chen

pmc-13420851.title: Associations between fatigue, burnout, and risk behaviors in mental health occupational therapists: a cross-sectional study of coping and substance use
pmc-13420851.creator: Miguel-Ángel Talavera-Valverde, Luis-Javier Márquez-Álvarez, Ana-Isabel Souto-Gómez
pmc-13420851.description: BackgroundOccupational therapists working in mental health services face sustained emotional demands, high workload, and clinical complexity, which may increase burnout risk. While Maslach’s three-dimensional model remains the gold standard for conceptualization, a gap persists in integrating physiological factors such as fatigue and behavioral risk outcomes within a theoretically derived framework in occupational therapy.

pmc-13550626.title: TiO2-facet-dependent reconstruction of Pt nanoparticles during CO oxidation
pmc-13550626.creator: Jihun Kim, Yunkyung Kim, Daewon Oh, Seokhyun Choung, Hyeongeon Lee, Hogyun Lee, Eonu Nam, Shinjae Lee, Jeongjin Kim, Sinmyung Yoon, Jeong Woo Han, Kwangjin An
pmc-13550626.description: Facet engineering of reducible oxide supports is a powerful strategy for tuning metal–support interactions. We show that this facet dependence extends beyond intrinsic support properties to govern the initial morphology and reaction-induced restructuring behaviour of supported Pt nanoparticles during CO oxidation. For ~1.

pmc-13569635.title: Safety Profile of Nebulized Ciprofloxacin‐Dexamethasone After Pediatric Airway Surgery
pmc-13569635.creator: Abbey L Landini, Cyrus W Abrahamson, Maya Frost, David Spielberg, Inbal Hazkani, Dana M Thompson, Jonathan B Ida, Sarah Maurrasse, Taher Valika
pmc-13569635.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the safety profile and patterns of use of nebulized ciprofloxacin–dexamethasone (CPD) in pediatric patients undergoing airway surgery.MethodsA retrospective chart review was performed of patients who underwent airway surgery at a tertiary pediatric center between 2019 and 2023 and received nebulized CPD 0.3%–0.1% postoperatively. Demographic, clinical, and procedural data were extracted. Exposure was defined as any postoperative nebulized administration.

pmc-13674463.title: Artificial intelligence driven diet‐intestinal microbiota‐host health integration: A four‐dimensional paradigm for advancing host wellness research
pmc-13674463.creator: Tianle He, Shuobo Zhang, Jiaxin Chen, Xiaoling Zheng, Jixin Zhao, Huifeng Li, Jiani Mao, Ju Luo, Jundan Zheng, Dengjun Ma, Lihong Wang, Junhui Liu, Wen Tian, Shuangming Yang, Chengli Liu, Ke Tian, Zhenguo Yang
pmc-13674463.description: The artificial intelligence (AI)‐driven diet‐intestinal microbiota‐host health integration paradigm has emerged as a novel framework for advancing host health research. Intestinal microbiota serves as a key mediator linking dietary signals to host homeostasis, while AI enables efficient integration of multi‐omics data to construct microbial metabolic models, identify interaction patterns across biological scales, and support prediction‐informed modulation of diet‐microbiota interactions.
